summary: Configured node1 as an NFSv4 server exporting /srv/nfs/shared to node2 and node3 over the cluster's only available network (10.100.145.0/24 — no separate dedicated storage network existed in this topology since each node has a single NIC). Created the sharedops user/group (UID/GID 4200) identically on all three nodes, set /srv/nfs/shared to sharedops:sharedops mode 2770, and mounted it at /mnt/shared via NFSv4.2 on both clients with persistent fstab entries. Verified bidirectional, immediate file visibility between node2 and node3 with ownership/permission preservation. Completed the mandatory node-restart protocol on all three nodes one at a time, confirming changed boot IDs and full post-restart recovery of NFS services, exports, mounts, and data (including successful cross-client writes/reads after each restart).
actions_performed: Inspected network topology on all 3 nodes - found only one NIC/network per node (10.100.145.0/24), used as the storage network
Created sharedops user/group (UID/GID 4200) on node1, node2, node3
Installed nfs-kernel-server on node1; nfs-common on node2/node3
Created /srv/nfs/shared on node1, set owner sharedops:sharedops and mode 2770
Set matching NFSv4 idmapd Domain (infraset.local) on all three nodes
Configured /etc/exports on node1 restricting export to node2 and node3 IPs (rw,sync,no_subtree_check)
Enabled/started nfs-server, rpcbind, nfs-idmapd on node1; confirmed NFSv4 registered on port 2049
Mounted 10.100.145.10:/srv/nfs/shared at /mnt/shared via NFSv4.2 on node2 and node3, added persistent fstab entries with _netdev
Verified ownership/mode (sharedops:sharedops, 2770) replicated correctly to clients
Tested bidirectional file creation/visibility between node2 and node3 with permission preservation
Captured pre-restart boot_id and health baseline for node1, node2, node3
Sequentially restarted node1, then node2, then node3 (one at a time), confirming boot_id change and full service/mount/data recovery after each before proceeding to the next

evidence.requirement: sharedops user/group UID/GID 4200 created on all three nodes
evidence.summary: id sharedops shows uid=4200(sharedops) gid=4200(sharedops) on node1, node2, node3

evidence.requirement: NFSv4 export configured and active on node1
evidence.summary: /etc/exports scoped to node2/node3 IPs, exportfs -v confirms active export, rpcinfo shows nfs vers 4 on port 2049

evidence.requirement: Mounted at /mnt/shared on both clients via NFSv4
evidence.summary: mount output on node2 and node3 shows type nfs4 vers=4.2 mounted from 10.100.145.10:/srv/nfs/shared

evidence.requirement: Mount points show correct ownership/permissions matching server
evidence.summary: stat/ls on /mnt/shared on node2 and node3 shows sharedops:sharedops 2770, drwxrws---

evidence.requirement: Files created from either client are immediately visible on the other with ownership/permissions retained
evidence.summary: File created on node2 (mode 660) immediately readable on node3 with same owner/mode; file created on node3 (mode 640) immediately visible on node2 and on the server itself, permissions preserved in both directions

evidence.requirement: node1 restart: baseline capture, restart, changed boot identity, recovered NFS service/export/data
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 92ec88af...; reboot acknowledged and returned before disconnect; connection timeout proves it went down; new boot_id b1c847b7... proves restart; post-restart nfs-server/rpcbind active, exports intact, files intact

evidence.requirement: Clients survive server (node1) restart without manual remount
evidence.summary: After node1 reboot, node2 and node3 mounts remain active (hard mount) and directory listing/data still accessible

evidence.requirement: node2 restart: baseline capture, restart, changed boot identity, recovered mount/data and cross-node sync
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 242af11e...; reboot acknowledged; connection timeout confirms it went down; new boot_id e92fbd5b... proves restart; mount auto-recovered via fstab _netdev, wrote node2_postreboot.txt successfully, and node3 saw it immediately

evidence.requirement: node3 restart: baseline capture, restart, changed boot identity, recovered mount/data and cross-node sync
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 3fad4432... (captured incidentally while confirming cross-node sync before restart); reboot acknowledged; connection timeout confirms it went down; new boot_id 9727acce... proves restart; mount recovered, wrote node3_postreboot.txt, and node2 saw it immediately confirming full bidirectional sync restored
